# Independent axis guards: an actual rank-two best-menu capacity obstruction

Continuous circuit rank TWO already permits strict failure of individual
Gamma_d capacity, even after optimizing over ALL actual active menus and
ALL nonnegative normal-dependent convex physical fields. The following
n=3,d=2 body gives an explicit certificate. It differs essentially from
the archived n=2 reflected-guard family: the three guard axes here have
no affine dependence, so retargeting a cap to another guard cannot retain
its minimum outside budget.

This is not an OC counterexample or a global bad-body minimum. Its unique
deepest source leaves unused parity classes. The separate replication
extension is being written by Optimal and is not needed for this result.

## 1. Exact lattice-complete body and actual covariance

Let T be the centroided triangle with vertices

    v1=(2,-1), v2=(-1,2), v3=(-1,-1), V=|T|=9/2.

Write lambda_i for its barycentrics. Let e1,e2,e3 be the standard integer
unit vectors of R^3. Fix

    0<sigma<=1/4,
    D_i=(1-sigma)v_i+sigma T,
    K_0=T, K_(+e_i)=K_(-e_i)=D_i.

The base hull is the integer cross-polytope {sum |z_i|<=1}. Its complete
lattice sample is exactly P={0,+-e1,+-e2,+-e3}. Every outer base is
exposed, and every D_i lies in T. Consequently the canonical convex hull
of these seven sampled fibers has exactly the stated fibers at all
sampled bases. The total mixed volume is

    M=V+6v, v=sigma^2 V.

Every D_i has within-fiber covariance sigma^2 Sigma_T. Therefore the
ACTUAL pooled within-fiber covariance is

    Sigma=kappa Sigma_T,
    kappa=(1+6sigma^4)/(1+6sigma^2).                 (1)

Since Var_T(lambda_i)=1/18, all canonical continuous normals
u_i=grad lambda_i have the same Gamma(u_i)=sqrt(kappa/18). Define the
actual outward width h by its barycentric width

    w=h sqrt(kappa/18),
    0<w<=min{1/100,sigma/6}.                         (2)

No independent norm or covariance is introduced.

## 2. A global outside quota for EVERY continuous direction

Let u!=0 and choose a vertex i maximizing u.v_i=M_u. As sum v_i=0,
M_u>0 and min_j u.v_j>=-2M_u. Hence for every X in D_i,

    u.X >= (1-sigma)M_u-2sigma M_u
          =(1-3sigma)M_u>0.                         (3)

Consider ANY base tilt a, and the cap through the middle source (0,0)
with margin a.z+u.X. At paired points (+e_i,X),(-e_i,X) the two margins
sum to 2u.X>0. At least one margin is positive, so its uniform outward
kernel value is one. Integrating paired points gives

    total outside capture >= v                       (4)

for EVERY u and EVERY a. This does not rely on near-canonical normals,
a stationary cap, or a prescribed finite menu.

For the canonical normal u_i, choose base normal a=e_i. On the i-th
guard pair, the +e_i fiber is fully captured and the -e_i fiber missed.
On every other guard, lambda_i<=sigma, so the margin is at most
sigma-1/3<=-1/12<-w. Thus this cap captures exactly one whole D_i and
misses all other outside fibers, attaining (4) with strict margins.

## 3. An exact all-normal classification of the OWN smoothed triangle minima

The only own minimizing continuous directions are the three canonical
u_i whenever w<=1/100. Here is a direct calculation, avoiding a local
stationarity or asymptotic classification assumption.

First suppose a direction has exactly one positive vertex projection.
By homogeneity write its three projections as

    a, -a(1+s)/2, -a(1-s)/2,
    a>0, |s|<=1.

The ordinary through-centroid cap fraction is 4/(9-s^2). Put eta=3w/2.
Using Var_T(u.X)=sum_j(u.v_j)^2/12 and (1), its outward width divided
by a is

    H_u/a=eta sqrt(1+s^2/3).                         (5)

If |s|<=1/2, this is at most2w<1/4, so the entire smoothing interval
preserves the one-vertex cut combinatorics. Averaging its ordinary
cap fraction over the outward displacement gives EXACTLY

    F_w(s)=4[1+eta sqrt(1+s^2/3)
                 +(eta^2/3)(1+s^2/3)]/(9-s^2).      (6)

The numerator is nondecreasing in s^2 and the denominator strictly
decreases. Thus (6) has its unique minimum at s=0. If |s|>=1/2, the
ordinary cap fraction is at least16/35; outward smoothing only increases
it.

If two vertex projections are nonnegative, scale the larger to1 and
write the other as b in [0,1], with third projection -1-b. The captured
ordinary fraction is

    1-(1+b)^2/[(2+b)(1+2b)] >=1/2,                  (7)

because 2(1+b)^2<=(2+b)(1+2b). Zero projections are included by continuity.

The canonical value, from (6) at zero, is

    q_h/V=4/9+2w/3+w^2/3
          <=4/9+1/150+1/30000<16/35.                (8)

Equations (6)--(8) cover ALL continuous directions and show equality
only at the three canonical vertex directions. The three threshold
coareas are positive and equal by the triangle's barycentric symmetry.
These are coareas for the displayed barycentric normals, or equivalently
for their common-Gamma normalization. The coordinate triangle is not
Euclidean regular; Euclidean unit-normal section lengths are not being
identified.

## 4. The unique actual deepest source and all active caps

By (4) and the own bound, every ambient cap through (0,0) has mass at
least q_h+v. The canonical caps constructed in Section2 attain it, so

    Q=q_h+v.                                        (9)

Pure-base closed caps through zero contain the whole middle fiber and
at least one member of each of the three reflected pairs, so their mass
is at least V+3v>Q. They are inactive.

The three displayed canonical caps have continuously balanced spanning
normals sum u_i=0. For every other middle mark X!=0 at least one u_i.X
is positive. Increasing the threshold of that fixed actual cap strictly
loses mass, initially through its proper own strip and thereafter by
monotonicity. Hence (0,0) uniquely maximizes depth on the middle fiber.
An exposed outer base can be isolated by a pure-base cap, giving depth
at most v<Q. Thus (0,0) is the UNIQUE actual global deepest source.

For ANY active cap at that source, its own mass is at least q_h and
outside mass at least v. Equality in (9) forces equality in both. By
Section3 its continuous direction must therefore be a canonical u_i.
For this direction the i-th pair already costs at least v, so every
other guard must be completely missed.

At paired i-th guard points, the continuous margin sum is strictly
positive by (3). If one kernel value is strictly between0 and1, its
paired value is1 and their sum is strictly greater than1. A positive
transition region would therefore make outside mass exceed v. The
two i-th guard kernels have zero transition volume. Since their
interiors are connected and the kernels continuous, each is constant0
or1 on its whole fiber, including its boundary. Exactly one is1.

We have classified EVERY actual active cap, with no restriction on its
base tilt:

    its direction is canonical i;
    it captures exactly one whole member of the i-th pair;
    it misses the remaining five outside fibers;
    all its transition coarea is on the own triangle. (10)

## 5. Every balanced menu has the same own profile and a guard ceiling1/3

The normalized continuous canonical normals have their unique positive
dependence with equal coefficients. Their own coareas are also equal,
and (10) gives zero outside coarea. Consequently EVERY balanced actual
response menu, allowing arbitrary repeated directions and arbitrary
active base tilts, has total response weight exactly1/3 in each of the
three direction classes.

On any given guard fiber only the corresponding direction class can
capture points, and each such cap captures the whole fiber or none.
Thus the actual guard profile is pointwise bounded above by1/3, on
EVERY guard facet normal, including all the extra internal parallel
facets. On the middle triangle the profile is independent of the menu.

This is the quantifier that the archived poor prescribed menu did not
control: optimizing the menu does not evade this classification.

## 6. Exact convex-order estimate for the two end strips

Let f>=0 be convex on [0,1] and 0<sigma<=1/2. Then

    int_([0,sigma] union [1-sigma,1]) f
          >=2sigma int_0^1 f.                       (11)

To prove it, replace f by its symmetric convex average
g(t)=[f(t)+f(1-t)]/2. This preserves both integrals. Symmetry and
convexity make g nonincreasing on [0,1/2]. The average on [0,sigma]
is therefore at least its average on [0,1/2]. Multiplying by2sigma
gives (11). No bound on f or its slope is used.

For each source edge F_i={lambda_i=0}, the two other vertices j,k have
guard patches D_j intersect F_i and D_k intersect F_i equal to its two
end strips of parameter length sigma. At every point X of the j patch,
the actual normal n_i occurs on both fibers at +-e_j, and convexity of
the full physical field gives

    2 Phi(n_i,0,X)
       <=Phi(n_i,+e_j,X)+Phi(n_i,-e_j,X).             (12)

Let I be its total middle boundary integral and E its total outside
boundary integral, summed over ALL actual normals. Integrating (12)
on the two disjoint patches of each edge and using (11) yields

    E>=4sigma I.                                    (13)

There is no boundary overcount: different j label different guard
fibers, and different i label different facets of each guard. Their
vertices have zero edge length. Every unlisted guard facet contributes
additional nonnegative cost to E and keeps the same profile ceiling1/3.

## 7. Uniform own-profile bound for arbitrarily concentrating convex fields

On F_i use t=lambda_j, lambda_k=1-t. For w<1/3 the own profile is

    W_h(t)=(1/3)[Psi((t-1/3)/w)+Psi((2/3-t)/w)].     (14)

At zero width,

    W_0=1/3+(1/3)1_[1/3,2/3].

Convexity gives 2f(t+1/3)<=f(t)+f(t+2/3), 0<=t<=1/3.
Integrating proves

    int W_0 f <= (4/9) int f.                        (15)

For positive w<=1/100, W_h-W_0 is nonnegative and supported on the
two ramp intervals [1/3-w,1/3] and [2/3,2/3+w], inside [1/4,3/4].
Its unweighted integral is exactly w/3. For every t in [1/4,3/4],
Jensen on [t-1/4,t+1/4] gives

    f(t)<=2 int_0^1 f.

Therefore the width error is bounded UNIFORMLY over the entire
nonnegative convex cone, including concentrating sequences:

    int W_h f <=(4/9+2w/3) int f.                    (16)

Apply (16) separately to the restriction of the physical field on each
source edge, retaining its actual normal and arc-length factor.

Optimal observed the following sharper exact version, which we use below:

    int W_h f <=(4/9+w/3) int f.                     (16a)

Indeed W_h is symmetric and nondecreasing on [0,1/2], while
g(t)=[f(t)+f(1-t)]/2 is symmetric and nonincreasing there. For s,t in
that half interval, [W_h(s)-W_h(t)][g(s)-g(t)]<=0. Double integration
gives the opposite Chebyshev inequality, hence
int W_h f<= (int W_h)(int f). The profile integral is exactly4/9+w/3.
This proof is likewise uniform over arbitrary concentrating convex
fields; no derivative or supremum bound is imposed.

## 8. A strict capacity upper bound for ALL menus and ALL physical fields

Let N be captured boundary integral, and D=I+E its total cost. Sections5
and7 imply

    N <=(4/9+w/3) I+(1/3)E.

Since E>=4sigma I and the first coefficient exceeds1/3, we obtain

    N/D <= [4/9+w/3+(4sigma)/3]/(1+4sigma)
         =4/9-[4sigma/9-w/3]/(1+4sigma).             (17)

If I=0 the ratio is at most1/3 and the same bound holds. Under (2),
the gap in (17) is at least sigma/[3(1+4sigma)], which is at least
sigma/9 because sigma<=1/4<1/2. Thus

    N <= (Gamma_2-sigma/9) D                         (18)

for EVERY balanced actual active menu and EVERY nonnegative convex
normal-dependent physical field. The bound includes all guard normals
and makes no compactness assumption on normalized fields.

An entirely explicit choice is

    sigma=1/4, w=1/1000,
    kappa=131/176, h=(1/1000)sqrt(3168/131).

Its rational sampled fibers and actual algebraic width satisfy every
displayed condition. The sharper bound (17) reads

    capacity <= 7/18+1/6000 <4/9.                    (19)

The only active continuous directions form a minimal positive rank-two
circuit. Thus the failure of individual best-menu Gamma capacity does
NOT intrinsically require continuous circuit rank at least three.

For comparison its capacity is at least1/3 exactly: use the displayed
menu a_i=e_i and the convex base-only field [2z_1-1]_+. It isolates
the exposed +e1 guard fiber, where that menu's profile is constantly1/3.
This also supplies the matching lower bound used in the replication
extension; no unproved generic hinge equality is required.

## 9. Why the older favorable guard construction does not transfer

The archived n=2 guard bases satisfy p1+p2+p3=0. That dependence supports
a cyclic joint coupling and forces a different outside quota; it allows
an active menu to retarget all continuous directions to one exposed
guard fiber. Here e1,e2,e3 are independent. Each canonical direction
already spends its entire minimum outside budget on its own reflected
pair. Equation (10) prohibits capturing any other guard while remaining
active. A favorable retargeted menu therefore does not exist.

The body has one deepest source and unused parity classes. Its normalized
depth is (q_h/V+sigma^2)/(1+6sigma^2), far above the OC target. The result
closes only the proposed universal individual rank-two payment route;
it leaves joint parity allocation and actual bad-body-minimum mechanisms
untouched.

# Independent axis guards: an actual rank-two best-menu capacity obstruction

**Unreplicated nonnegative physical-field capacity falls below gamma_2**

In the attained pure outward-smoothed model, the independent-axis triangle-guard construction has n=3,d=2. For 0<sigma<=1/4 and 0<w<=min(1/100,sigma/6), every actual balanced active menu and every nonnegative continuous normal-dependent physical field convex in the ambient point, with positive total boundary cost D, has efficiency N/D <= [4/9+w/3+(4sigma)/3]/(1+4sigma) <= 4/9-sigma/9. The choice sigma=1/4,w=1/1000 gives N/D<=7/18+1/6000<4/9. This obstructs the individual nonnegative-field gamma_2 capacity claim; it does not assert the replicated below-1/e bound or refute ordinary OC.

Scope limits: Only nonnegative-field capacity is obstructed. The bodies have unused source parity and admit signed descent; they do not contradict OC or stationary minimality.
